An Org file can remain the original working document. The publishing copy can be generated as Markdown or Quarto Markdown (`.qmd`).

## The simple workflow

1. Write and revise the note in Org mode.
2. Export it to Markdown with Pandoc or Emacs.
3. Add a short YAML header containing the page title, description, and categories.
4. Preview the site and check code blocks, equations, images, and internal links.
5. Commit the source and publish the generated website.

For example, Pandoc can create a Markdown starting point:

```bash
pandoc note.org --from=org --to=gfm --output=note.md
```

The resulting file is already valid input for Quarto. Rename it to `.qmd` only when Quarto-specific features are useful.

## Minimal page header

```yaml
---
title: "A useful title"
description: "One sentence explaining the page."
categories: [Emacs, workflow]
---
```

::: {.callout-note}
Quarto accepts ordinary Markdown files. There is no requirement to rewrite every tutorial into Quarto-specific syntax.
:::

## Where a new tutorial goes

```text
tutorials/
  updating-docker-apps.qmd
  downloading-large-datasets.qmd
  large-datasets.md
```

`tutorials/` is flat — subject is a `categories:` tag, not a folder. The
one exception is a genuine multi-part course (several ordered pages that
belong together), which gets its own subfolder, e.g. `tutorials/hpc/`.
Either way, the Tutorials listing discovers new pages automatically, so
adding one does not require redesigning the site.
